title: Put the whole command surface in the session preamble
action: Render a new '### Command surface' section into the session preamble, built from the EMBEDDED registry (crate::registry::REGISTRY_PAYLOAD via the existing catalog access — never a checked-in copy, which would drift the moment a verb changes). One line per command, path-sorted for byte-stability: '<command name>: --<flag>*:<type-abbrev> ...', where * marks a required flag and the type abbreviation is the schema type's first three letters. Omit the 'json' flag from every line and say once in the section header that nearly every command accepts --json — it appears on 130 of 142 commands and repeating it costs about 1KB for no information. A command with no flags beyond --json renders its name alone, never a dangling colon. Place the section after '### Standard commands' and before '### Doc links': the closing trailer's exact bytes are pinned by an ends_with assertion in session_preamble/tests.rs, so nothing may be appended at the end. Tests: the section renders with a known fixture; required flags carry * and optional ones do not; the string '--json' appears nowhere inside the section; a flagless command renders without a trailing colon; the preamble still ends with the same trailer bytes; and one budget assertion that the whole section stays under 9000 characters, so a future verb explosion is caught rather than silently paid for on every session.

truths: Every registry command appears with its flags, required ones marked
--json appears nowhere in the section body
The preamble trailer bytes are unchanged
The section is built from the embedded registry, never a copied list
A character budget guards the section's size
The full declared test suite is green

trace.outcome: Render the whole registry into a new Command surface preamble section, path-sorted, --json omitted per-line and noted once in the header
